concept.title: Images
concept.shortdesc: An element of your XML can show an image from a file. This chapter explains how to turn an element into an image, how to size it and how to fit it in its box. The images reference at the end lists the properties.

conbody.p: XML has no element for images, so the stylesheet decides which elements are images. An element whose content is an image is a replaced element: CSSMedia shows the image in its place and ignores what the element contains. Most vocabularies keep the name of the file in an attribute, and the stylesheet reads it from there.
CSSMedia reads these image formats, and it knows the format from the content of the file, not from its name:

row.entry: All color types and bit depths, interlaced files, transparency and the color profile of the file.
Baseline, extended and progressive files of 8 bits, in gray, RGB or CMYK, with the color profile of the file.
Lossy and lossless files, with transparency and the color profile of the file.
Drawings, which CSSMedia draws as vector graphics. SVG explains how to write them.

conbody.p: The same files work as the images of a background-image, which Backgrounds explains. An image is a picture in the PDF: it does not move, and its pixels are not text.
The element names in the examples of this chapter, such as figure and src, are placeholders. Use the names that occur in your XML.
